content:
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Primary endpoint analysis lacks estimand attributes",
      "quote": "The pCR rate per independent central pathology review along with 95% exact confidence interval will be calculated using Clopper-Pearson method",
      "page": 74,
      "section": "11.5.3.1",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The primary analysis description does not specify the estimand attributes: population (FAS is stated elsewhere but not here), variable definition (pCR rate), intercurrent events handling (e.g., patients who do not undergo surgery), and summary measure (rate with CI). The estimand is incomplete.",
      "fix": "Add a full estimand description for the primary endpoint, including handling of intercurrent events such as patients who do not have surgery or die before surgery."
    },
    {
      "title": "Secondary endpoints lack analysis methods",
      "quote": "Change in planned surgery will",
      "page": 74,
      "section": "11.5.3.2",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The text cuts off mid-sentence, and no analysis method is provided for the secondary endpoints 'Change in surgical plan' and 'Change in post-surgical management plan'. These endpoints are listed in Section 4.2 but have no statistical analysis description.",
      "fix": "Complete the sentence and provide a detailed statistical analysis for change in surgical plan and post-surgical management plan, including how the change will be measured and summarized."
    },
    {
      "title": "Exploratory endpoints lack analysis methods",
      "quote": "The exploratory endpoints are: Patterns of failure in patients with local, regional, or distant disease recurrence as measured by descriptive statistics",
      "page": 26,
      "section": "4.3",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Exploratory endpoints such as patterns of failure, cost changes, ADA, and quality of life are listed but no statistical analysis methods are described in Section 11.5 for these endpoints.",
      "fix": "Add analysis methods for all exploratory endpoints, including descriptive statistics, cost analysis, immunogenicity analysis, and QoL analysis."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing handling of intercurrent events for EFS/DFS/OS",
      "quote": "Event free survival (EFS), DFS and OS will be summarized using Kaplan-Meier method.",
      "page": 74,
      "section": "11.5.3.2",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The analysis for time-to-event endpoints does not specify how intercurrent events (e.g., death without event, new primary cancer, or treatment discontinuation) are handled in the definition of EFS and DFS. This is a key estimand attribute.",
      "fix": "Define the event definitions and censoring rules for EFS, DFS, and OS, including handling of competing risks and intercurrent events."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing multiplicity control for secondary endpoints",
      "quote": "The secondary endpoints are: mPR rate assessed by independent central pathology review",
      "page": 26,
      "section": "4.2",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol does not describe any multiplicity adjustment for testing multiple secondary endpoints. This could lead to inflated Type I error.",
      "fix": "Add a section on multiplicity control for secondary endpoints, specifying the testing hierarchy or adjustment method."
    },
    {
      "title": "Sample size inconsistency between 72 and 76 patients",
      "quote": "Seventy-two (72) patients will be required to provide 90% power to reject a null hypothesis of a pCR rate of 25% at a 2-sided significance level of 0.05 if the true pCR rate is 44%.",
      "page": 72,
      "section": "11.2",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The sample size justification states 72 patients are required, but then says the sample size will be increased by 5% to 76 patients. The text is inconsistent: 5% of 72 is 3.6, not 4, and the final sample size is 76, which is a 5.6% increase. Also, the power calculation is based on 72, but the CI table uses 76.",
      "fix": "Clarify the exact sample size calculation: state the number of patients needed for power (72) and the inflation factor (e.g., 5% rounding to 76) and ensure consistency throughout."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing analysis for primary endpoint in interim analysis",
      "quote": "No interim analysis is planned for the primary endpoint. After all patients have completed Part 1 of the study (Table 2), an interim clinical study report (CSR) may be written to describe the analysis results for the primary endpoint.",
      "page": 32,
      "section": "6.2",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The text says 'No interim analysis is planned' but then describes an interim CSR that will describe the primary endpoint results. This is contradictory and could confuse the analysis plan.",
      "fix": "Clarify whether the interim CSR is a formal interim analysis or just a descriptive report, and specify if any statistical testing or stopping rules apply."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing analysis for health-related quality of life endpoint",
      "quote": "Health-related quality of life, as assessed using the EORTC QLQ-C30",
      "page": 26,
      "section": "4.3",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The QoL endpoint is listed but no analysis method is described in the statistical plan. The protocol does not specify how QoL data will be scored, summarized, or compared.",
      "fix": "Add a description of the QoL analysis, including scoring rules, handling of missing data, and summary measures."
    }
  ]
}
